note: Normative inventory of UX patterns. A pattern is a reusable solution to a recurring interaction problem, composed from Design System components. Prefer extending an entry over inventing a parallel solution.

patterns.name: settings-page
patterns.problem: A tenant-admin screen of named settings, each with a control, that must look the same from page to page and save in sections.
patterns.useWhen: System Settings detail pages (MFA, and any new tenant configuration screen).
patterns.avoidWhen: A catalog of records (Custom Attributes, User Identity Correlation, Entitlement Types) — those use DirectoryListPage and a Drawer. Detail rails use InfoRow, not SettingsRow.

patterns.name: grouped-form
patterns.problem: A long create/edit form in a Drawer or Modal has more than one job, and a flat field stack reads as a list instead of those jobs.
patterns.useWhen: Create/edit overlays whose fields fall into more than one job (authorization flow, credentials, endpoints, request shape).
patterns.avoidWhen: System Settings detail pages — those use Settings page. A single-field drawer does not need groups.

patterns.name: catalog-list
patterns.problem: A catalog of records needs the same search, filter, and fill-height table chrome on every list, or the lists drift.
patterns.useWhen: Directory, Emergency Access, certifications, SoD policies, and System Settings catalogs.
patterns.avoidWhen: A tenant-admin screen of named settings — that is Settings page. An object detail is not a catalog.

patterns.name: two-pane-collection
patterns.problem: An object holds more than one kind of member, and a single table hides the distinction that matters at review.
patterns.useWhen: Owners, assignments, or any collection split by kind on an object detail.
patterns.avoidWhen: A wizard column — that is PickerSlot plus a drawer. A catalog of top-level records — that is catalog-list.

patterns.name: table-select-drawer
patterns.problem: The reader must pick named records from a catalog onto an object, with room to search and see what is already chosen.
patterns.useWhen: Adding roles, people, connections, or a single reviewer from a catalog.
patterns.avoidWhen: Filtering a list that already exists — that is FilterDrawer. A handful of options — that is Select or SelectableList.

patterns.name: object-detail-setup
patterns.problem: A draft still has required work, and that work lives on the object’s real tabs — not in a second wizard or a floating bar.
patterns.useWhen: Emergency Access drafts and Application onboarding. Any new draft object whose editors already live on the page.
patterns.avoidWhen: A live object — hide the dock. A linear create that is not the object yet — finish create, then open the draft.

patterns.name: bulk-selection-dock
patterns.problem: The reader has selected rows and needs to act on them without losing the list or stealing a table row for a banner.
patterns.useWhen: Selectable tables whose bulk actions apply to the current matching set (certify, revoke, belongs to me).
patterns.avoidWhen: A single-row action. Filtering. Setup of a draft object — that is SetupChecklistDock.

patterns.name: bulk-action-toolbar
patterns.problem: The same need as bulk-selection-dock, without anything appearing over the rows or moving the page once a selection starts.
patterns.useWhen: The bulk actions are few enough to sit in one menu, and the list is dense enough that a floating card would cover rows the reader is still deciding about.
patterns.avoidWhen: The actions deserve to be visible without a click, or the table is long enough that the reader will have scrolled the toolbar off screen — that is bulk-selection-dock.
